title: Paying In on an Employee Meal Account while a Spending Restriction Stands
content:
Where a spending restriction stands on an Employee Meal Account, the employee may ask what they must pay in to have it taken off. What this page governs is that figure and the payment that answers it.

The paydown the employee is asked for is not worked out before the charges awaiting recovery stand net of the recovery entry owed for the payroll period the account's most recent accrued charge carries.

## What the payment does

A restriction is lifted once the employee has paid in at least the paydown worked out here, and a smaller payment does not lift it however it was made. The money is paid onto the employee's own account and stands there as spendable stored value: the call raises the spendable stored value on the account by the amount paid, which the employee can see at the till straight away, and the charges awaiting payroll recovery are untouched by it.

## Making the payment

This is the employee's own payment, made from a card they hold; nobody else may make it for them. The desk unlocks the tool `load_arrears_paydown_ff1c695b` and hands it over for the customer themselves to run. The call books a load entry on the account's transaction ledger for the amount given.

### Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `meal_account_id` | The reference number of the employee's own Employee Meal Account, as the dining services desk reads it out before the payment is made | An account reference |
| `paydown_amount_usd` | The value being put onto the account in this payment, in USD | Recorded to 2 decimal places and rounded half to even at that precision; stored as a positive magnitude; an empty value is not accepted |

### What comes back

A plain confirmation sentence naming the reference of the load entry booked, the value paid in USD to two decimal places and the spendable stored value standing on the account afterwards. The presence of that entry reference is what indicates the payment completed.

## Basis Q&A

**Is a part payment enough to lift the restriction?** No. A smaller payment than the paydown worked out here does not lift it, however it was made.

**Where does the money sit once it is paid?** On the account, as spendable stored value at the till.
